objective: Refuse a World Model append that would take a run past the read model's 10,000-event ceiling, so the write boundary never reports a durable stream the Dashboard reader rejects, using one declared ceiling instead of two copies of the number.
acceptance: exactly 10000 valid events remain storable and readable
the append that would make it 10001 is refused before it becomes durable, with a stable reason naming the run, the current count and the limit
the refusal leaves the stored run unchanged and replayable at 10000 events, with no truncation, merge or silent drop
an exact retry of an already-stored event remains a no-op and does not count as a new event, even at the ceiling
the reader and the writer use one declared ceiling: the World Model store imports MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN from the read model instead of restating the number
a regression test demonstrates the current over-limit success and the fixed refusal
evidence: row counts before and after the refused append: 10000 stored, 10001 attempted, 10000 stored after
the append refusal message naming the run, the count and the ceiling
a replay of the unchanged 10000-event run through SQLiteEventStore.list_run
the read model accepting the 10000-event stream and rejecting the 10001-event stream
pytest, Ruff and Task Packet boundary output
stop_conditions: the fix would delete or truncate an existing event
a larger supported ceiling requires a read-model resource design that is out of scope
event schema, robot-control or hardware behaviour would have to change
the read model would have to be duplicated to make the number shared
